(a) Onset is established: memory_pct is flat ~47.7-48.5% for the entire pre-deploy day 03-20 and begins climbing in the 03-21T01:40Z bucket (51.77%), within ~1.7h of the 03-21T00:00Z deploy (F31); it then forms a near-identical per-restart saw-tooth at a constant ~2%/h slope that resets only at each restart, with no external trigger and flat request_rate (F32/F33/F35/F36). (b) Every competing origin with a verified change is now contradicted by direct measurement, not assumption: cfg-2410 produced no broker-side replay (messages_in_per_s flat 2230-2410), no under-replication/rebalance (under_replicated_partitions 0.0, cpu flat ~35%), and no anomaly in the co-tenant shared-Kafka consumer settlement-service (memory flat, 0 restarts, lag normal, 0 WARN+ logs) (F25-F30); no producer change exists at all (F19-F24); and no notification-service retune exists (F3/F15/F24). Temporal order is tight and the negative/positive facts are coherent: cache entries rise monotonically with 0 evictions (F11), heap/GC warnings appear only at cycles' peaks, first-ever at 03-21T21:37Z (F36/F11), the kill at 19:59:21Z follows the 98.44% peak immediately (F7/F8), and lag spikes AT the OOM then recovers within 30 min (F10). Two residual weaknesses keep this below 0.9: the single causal hop 'email delay is a consequence of the restart, not a traffic surge' is ASSUMED with no lag/error-rate correlation for the email path, and cache unboundedness is inferred from entry count + 0 evictions rather than confirmed by a size cap/TTL. Neither is a plausible competing origin, so they cap confidence rather than block the verdict. Given 15 tool calls remain and two low-cost, directly discriminating queries exist, this is best accepted with a capped confidence; no rollback was attempted, so the discriminating intervention evidence is absent but the mechanism chain does not depend on it.

tasks.answer: The change set does not support a Kafka-replay trigger: the only change near the incident is cfg-2410 (kafka log.retention.ms 7d->3d) at 2026-03-23T18:00Z, and the observable onset — memory ramp and OOM — starts BEFORE it or unrelated to replay volume (memory already >83.69% at window start via T1, TemplateCache growth from 14:30Z, GC warnings from 18:34:46Z). Meanwhile the notification-service memory-footprint-affecting change (dep-5402 in-memory TemplateCache, 2026-03-21T00:00Z) is still live and never rolled back, predating all three OOMs. Retention reduction (7d->3d) actually deletes old segments and cannot itself cause a replay; the lag spike coincides with the OOM (19:45Z) rather than preceding it. Prior OOM/OOMKilled precedents for notification-service were NOT found in history (only lag/rebalance leads HIST-104/HIST-112, and an unrelated cache-cold-storm HIST-107); so the cache build-up root cause has no historical precedent to compare, which itself is notable.

tasks.answer: The memory ramp is a per-restart saw-tooth, not a single monotonic climb with an 18:00Z trigger. The first ramp begins at the deployment hour: memory_pct is flat at ~48% for all of 2026-03-20, then starts climbing in the 2026-03-21T01:40Z bucket (51.77%) immediately after dep-5402 v3.8.0 (2026-03-21T00:00Z). It climbs steadily to ~92.8% by 2026-03-21T20:00Z, is reset by OOM restart #1 (~22:00Z), then climbs again from ~49% (2026-03-21T23:40Z) to ~94% by 2026-03-22T19:50Z, reset by restart #2 (~22:00Z), and climbs a third identical time from ~52% (2026-03-22T23:30Z) to 98.44% at 2026-03-23T19:30Z before restart #3 (~19:59Z). Each cycle resumes climbing as soon as traffic flows after the restart, with no external trigger. The rate is constant (~2%/hour) across all three cycles and request_rate is flat all week (mean 140.83 req/s), so it is not traffic-driven. There is NO 18:00Z (03-23) inflection: the zoomed series rises smoothly through 18:00Z (91.67% at 17:25Z -> 93.67% at 17:50Z -> 93.51% at 18:15Z) with no slope change. This supports H1's mechanism (in-heap growth resuming at restart) and shows the Kafka cfg-2410 change at 18:00Z is temporally decoupled from the memory ramp, which had been running for ~2 days.

critiques.summary: H1 (dep-5402 in-heap TemplateCache) is the best-supported origin: the deploy predates all three OOMs, it is the only change that raises the in-process memory footprint, cache entries grow monotonically with 0 evictions, memory ramps to 98.4% and the kill at 19:59:21Z falls immediately after the peak, while lag spikes AT the OOM and recovers within 30 min. H2's Kafka-replay trigger is correctly rejected on timing (restarts #1/#2 predate cfg-2410; memory already ramp at window start). However, two evidence gaps remain that are cheap to close and could change ranking or force a lower confidence cap: (a) the memory ramp is asserted to start at/before 14:00Z but no data before 14:00Z was ever retrieved, so the 'onset' is not actually established — without it the 03-21 cache deploy is only inferentially linked to the ramp; (b) the only competing explanation with a *verified* change (shared-Kafka cfg-2410) was dismissed partly on the assumption that retention reduction cannot produce a replay, and the other shared-Kafka consumer (settlement-service) was never checked — if it also shows an anomaly at 18:00Z the shared change gains weight. Producer history (order/payment) is a lower-priority confirmation, but it was never fetched and could in principle add load. Also note the cache-unboundedness is inferred, not inspected (no code/size-cap/TTL evidence), so 0.74 is above what the evidence supports.

challenges.issue: Onset time is NOT established. The chain claims the ramp 'begins' at/before 83.28% at 14:00Z, but the queried window starts at 14:00Z — no data before that was retrieved. Without a pre-14:00Z baseline, the memory ramp cannot be shown to start after the 03-21 deploy, and the 'no daily baseline' assumption admits a routine traffic curve is not excluded. The 03-21 deploy-to-ramp link is therefore inferential, not verified.

Cache unboundedness is inferred from '0 evictions' + the deploy description, not from code/size-cap/TTL evidence. The strongest available confirmation — does heap/deploy correlate as a per-restart saw-tooth that resumes with traffic — was never queried.

One chain hop ('email delays are the restart consequence, not a traffic surge') has no evidence. This is a user-visible symptom claim, not load-bearing for the root cause, so it is minor with respect to origin but should be stated as an assumption.

Rejected partly on the speculative assertion that retention reduction 'cannot' cause a replay, and with NO Kafka-side telemetry (no messages_in_per_s, no WARN/ERROR logs). The shared-Kafka trigger was eliminated by notification-service-local timing, not by direct contradiction of the Kafka mechanism; the other shared consumer (settlement-service) was never examined, so 'shared change affected only one consumer' is unverified.

Dismissed on a positive argument (keyed cache wouldn't grow with volume) plus absence of evidence — but the absence was inferred from an incomplete search: producer (order-service/payment-service) deployment history was never retrieved due to budget exhaustion. This is the strongest form of 'absence inferred from incomplete result'.

Correctly rejected; F3/F15 cover only the recorded 03-01..03-23 scope and the analysts themselves flag a possible out-of-scope change. Low residual risk given H1 has a positive mechanism, but the rejection rests on a scope-bounded query.

evidence_requests.rationale: This is the decisive test for H1 vs H2: if old-gen/heap starts climbing immediately after the 03-21 deploy and shows post-restart saw-tooth recovery with no 18:00Z inflection, the cache origin is confirmed and the shared-Kafka trigger is excluded on evidence rather than inference. It also supplies the missing pre-14:00Z baseline the chain currently assumes.

evidence_requests.question: Query settlement-service (the other shared-Kafka consumer) and kafka broker-side telemetry for 2026-03-23T14:00-23:59Z: settlement-service memory_pct / restart count / consumer-lag-proxy, plus kafka messages_in_per_s and under_replicated_partitions. Did anything on the shared Kafka path or on settlement-service deviate around the 18:00Z cfg-2410 change?
evidence_requests.rationale: cfg-2410 is a shared-component change; H2 is currently rejected without any Kafka-side or peer-consumer evidence. If settlement-service or broker metrics are clean through 18:00-20:00Z, the shared-Kafka explanation is genuinely contradicted; if either shows a coincident anomaly, H2 regains weight and the ranking changes.

evidence_requests.question: Retrieve deployment and release history for order-service and payment-service (the Kafka producers) over 2026-03-01..2026-03-23, and any producer-side message-size/volume or payload-schema change records in that window.
evidence_requests.rationale: H3 is rejected partly by an absence of evidence that was inferred from a query that never completed (budget exhausted). A producer change is the only remaining route by which the shared-topic load could contribute to the memory/lag pattern, so confirming or eliminating it is the cheapest way to close the alternative space.

critiques.summary: H1 (dep-5402 v3.8.0 in-heap TemplateCache) is now well supported end-to-end, and the two blocking gaps from round 1 are closed. (a) Onset is established: memory_pct is flat ~47.7-48.5% for the entire pre-deploy day 03-20 and begins climbing in the 03-21T01:40Z bucket (51.77%), within ~1.7h of the 03-21T00:00Z deploy (F31); it then forms a near-identical per-restart saw-tooth at a constant ~2%/h slope that resets only at each restart, with no external trigger and flat request_rate (F32/F33/F35/F36). (b) Every competing origin with a verified change is now contradicted by direct measurement, not assumption: cfg-2410 produced no broker-side replay (messages_in_per_s flat 2230-2410), no under-replication/rebalance (under_replicated_partitions 0.0, cpu flat ~35%), and no anomaly in the co-tenant shared-Kafka consumer settlement-service (memory flat, 0 restarts, lag normal, 0 WARN+ logs) (F25-F30); no producer change exists at all (F19-F24); and no notification-service retune exists (F3/F15/F24). Temporal order is tight and the negative/positive facts are coherent: cache entries rise monotonically with 0 evictions (F11), heap/GC warnings appear only at cycles' peaks, first-ever at 03-21T21:37Z (F36/F11), the kill at 19:59:21Z follows the 98.44% peak immediately (F7/F8), and lag spikes AT the OOM then recovers within 30 min (F10). Two residual weaknesses keep this below 0.9: the single causal hop 'email delay is a consequence of the restart, not a traffic surge' is ASSUMED with no lag/error-rate correlation for the email path, and cache unboundedness is inferred from entry count + 0 evictions rather than confirmed by a size cap/TTL. Neither is a plausible competing origin, so they cap confidence rather than block the verdict. Given 15 tool calls remain and two low-cost, directly discriminating queries exist, this is best accepted with a capped confidence; no rollback was attempted, so the discriminating intervention evidence is absent but the mechanism chain does not depend on it.

challenges.issue: The final hop 'email delays (~25 min) are the consequence of the restart-induced consumer outage rather than a traffic surge' is ASSUMED, with no email-path telemetry. It is a minor hop for the root cause (email delay is the user-visible effect, not part of the OOM mechanism) but it means the stated business impact is uncorroborated.

Cache unboundedness is inferred (monotonic entry count, 0 evictions, noroll-back) rather than verified by code inspection of a size cap/TTL in v3.8.0. If the cache had a cap, the 0-eviction observation would be unexplained, so this is low risk, but it is still an inference underpinning the mechanism.
No rollback/disable of dep-5402 was attempted, so the strongest discriminating intervention is absent. Evidence is entirely observational (predecessor correlation + mechanism telemetry).

H2 is rejected emphatically but rests partly on inference that retention reduction deletes segments rather than replaying them; broker-side rebalance counters were unavailable. However the mechanism is independently contradicted by flat ingest, 0 under-replication, and a clean co-tenant consumer, so this is not blocking.

Producer-side elimination is by absence of recorded changes (F19-F24), not by direct measurement of shared-topic ingest volume per producer. The queue-consume edge is single (F4), so per-producer attribution is not derivable; risk is low given flat broker ingest and the cache-key structure.
